Sony Joins Lionsgate to Co-Finance and Distribute Destin Daniel Cretton’s Live-Action ‘Naruto’ Adaptation

04 Nov 2026, 01:17 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Entertainment Desk · Source: deadline.com

1 min read

Key takeawaysSony Pictures has secured international distribution rights and agreed to co-finance the upcoming live-action adaptation of the global manga franchise Naruto. The project is a collaboration with Lionsgate, which has officially greenlit the film.

Studio Collaboration and Production Timeline

Sony Pictures has secured international distribution rights and agreed to co-finance the upcoming live-action adaptation of the global manga franchise *Naruto*. The project is a collaboration with Lionsgate, which has officially greenlit the film.

Filmmaker Destin Daniel Cretton remains attached to write and direct the feature. According to reported production schedules, principal photography is slated to begin in the spring.

Division of Responsibilities

The distribution and production responsibilities are divided between the two major studios:

  • Lionsgate: Leading development and production while handling domestic distribution rights.
  • Sony Pictures: Managing international distribution and co-financing the feature.

Franchise Background and Creative Team

Masashi Kishimoto’s original *Naruto* manga has achieved substantial commercial reach, selling over 250 million copies across more than 60 countries and territories. Its corresponding anime adaptation has been broadcast in over 145 countries, solidifying its status as a multibillion-dollar property.

Reports indicate that manga creator Masashi Kishimoto is closely involved with the film's production. The producing team features:

  • Avi Arad, Ari Arad, and Emmy Yu for Arad Productions
  • Destin Daniel Cretton and Jeyun Munford for Hisako

How to Verify Original Announcements

Industry announcements regarding production timelines, casting, and distribution agreements are typically verified through official studio press releases and filings reported by major trade publications such as Deadline, Variety, and The Hollywood Reporter.
